limit_order_match_in_progress.meaning: a limit order match (partial or full) is being processed in _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder
limit_order_match_in_progress.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

matched_base_amount.meaning: matched base amount of the limit order match
matched_base_amount.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

matched_quote_amount.meaning: matched quote amount of the limit order match
matched_quote_amount.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

matched_amounts_bitwise_and.meaning: bitwise AND of matched base amount and matched quote amount, zero exactly when they have no overlapping 1-bits
matched_amounts_bitwise_and.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

one_sided_trade.meaning: the trade is one-sided: one side receives tokens without sending any, the only case the zero-cost trade check must reject
one_sided_trade.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

legitimate_trade_completes.meaning: the legitimate limit order match whose matched amounts have disjoint bits completes without a misleading zero-cost rejection error
legitimate_trade_completes.checkpoint: after the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

assumptions: The zero-cost trade check is the check applied during the limit order match processing described by the report.
A match whose matched base and quote amounts have no overlapping 1-bits is a legitimate trade per the report's intent.

unresolved.description: The report does not state the exact revert condition or error text (omitted code lines 503-504 and 544-545), so the misleading-error observable is bound only as a Boolean completion outcome rather than a specific revert predicate.

limitations: Caller identity and authorization for triggering the match are not specified by the report and are not encoded.
Whether matched amounts are attacker-chosen or arise naturally is not stated; the plan encodes only the disjoint-bits scenario.
The bitwise-AND observable is a symbolic encoding of the report's 'no overlapping 1-bits' relation; concrete values are deferred to code binding.
The one-sided-trade qualifier is a report-grounded Boolean because the report gives no numeric definition of one-sidedness.
